ورد الصباح والمساء من حصن المسلم بتخريجه: The morning and evening remembrances from Hisn al-Muslim with their sources, shown at the right time for your city.

Its time is now; best is soon after dawn.
يمتد وقتها عند بعض العلماء إلى العصر، فإ: Some scholars extend its time until Asr; if you missed it, recite it now.
أفضل وقتها الآن: من العصر إلى غروب الشمس: Its best time is now: from Asr until sunset.
وقتها الآن، ويمتد عند كثير من العلماء إل: Its time is now; many scholars extend it into the early night.
يمتد وقتها عند كثير من العلماء في الليل،: Many scholars extend its time into the night; the morning remembrances begin at dawn.
قال الله تعالى: ﴿فَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ حِي: Allah says: “So glorify Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning” (al-Rum 30:17), and: “Glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting” (Qaf 50:39).

§a.kursi.m: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast. Then Ayat al-Kursi (al-Baqarah 2:255).
§a.kursi.v: Whoever recites it in the morning is protected from the jinn until evening, and whoever recites it in the evening is protected from them until morning.
§a.kursi.s: Al-Hakim (1/562); graded authentic by al-Albani in Sahih al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (1/273)
§a.baqara.m: The last two verses of Surat al-Baqarah (2:285–286).
§a.baqara.v: Whoever recites the last two verses of Surat al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him.
§a.quls.m: Surat al-Ikhlas, Surat al-Falaq and Surat al-Nas, each beginning with the Basmala.
§a.quls.v: Whoever recites them three times in the morning and in the evening, they will suffice him against everything.
§a.quls.s: Abu Dawud (5082) and al-Tirmidhi (3575); see Sahih al-Tirmidhi (3/182)
§a.mulk.m: We have entered the morning, and all sovereignty belongs to Allah. Praise is to Allah. There is no god but Allah alone, without partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this day and the good of what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this day and the evil of what follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the misery of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave.
§a.mulk.e: We have entered the evening, and all sovereignty belongs to Allah. Praise is to Allah. There is no god but Allah alone, without partner; His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this night and the good of what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this night and the evil of what follows it. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from laziness and the misery of old age. My Lord, I seek refuge in You from punishment in the Fire and punishment in the grave.
§a.mulk.v: The Prophet ﷺ used to say it every morning and evening.
§a.bika.m: O Allah, by You we enter the morning and by You we enter the evening, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the resurrection.
§a.bika.e: O Allah, by You we enter the evening and by You we enter the morning, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the final return.
§a.bika.v: The Prophet ﷺ taught it to his Companions.
§a.bika.s: Al-Tirmidhi (3391) and Abu Dawud (5068); see Sahih al-Tirmidhi (3/142)
§a.sayyid.m: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I keep Your covenant and promise as best I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You.
§a.sayyid.v: The master supplication for forgiveness: whoever says it with conviction in the evening and dies that night enters Paradise, and likewise in the morning.
§a.ushhid.m: O Allah, I have entered the morning calling You to witness, and calling the bearers of Your Throne, Your angels and all Your creation to witness, that You are Allah, there is no god but You alone without partner, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Messenger.
§a.ushhid.e: O Allah, I have entered the evening calling You to witness, and calling the bearers of Your Throne, Your angels and all Your creation to witness, that You are Allah, there is no god but You alone without partner, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Messenger.
§a.ushhid.v: Whoever says it four times, Allah frees him from the Fire.
§a.ushhid.s: Abu Dawud (5069); Ibn Baz graded its chain good in Tuhfat al-Akhyar
§a.nima.m: O Allah, whatever blessing I or any of Your creation have this morning is from You alone, without partner. To You is the praise and to You is the thanks.
§a.nima.e: O Allah, whatever blessing I or any of Your creation have this evening is from You alone, without partner. To You is the praise and to You is the thanks.
§a.nima.v: Whoever says it in the morning has given thanks for his day, and whoever says it in the evening has given thanks for his night.
§a.nima.s: Abu Dawud (5073); Ibn Baz graded its chain good in Tuhfat al-Akhyar
§a.afini.m: O Allah, grant me wellbeing in my body. O Allah, grant me wellbeing in my hearing. O Allah, grant me wellbeing in my sight. There is no god but You. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disbelief and poverty, and I seek refuge in You from the punishment of the grave. There is no god but You.
§a.afini.v: The Prophet ﷺ used to supplicate with it three times every morning and evening.
§a.afini.s: Abu Dawud (5090) and Ahmad (5/42); Ibn Baz graded its chain good in Tuhfat al-Akhyar
§a.hasbi.m: Allah is sufficient for me; there is no god but He. In Him I put my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne.
§a.hasbi.v: Whoever says it seven times in the morning and evening, Allah will suffice him in whatever concerns him of this world and the Hereafter.
§a.hasbi.s: Abu Dawud (5081) as a statement of Abu al-Darda; Shuayb and Abd al-Qadir al-Arnaut graded its chain authentic in their edition of Zad al-Maad (2/376)
§a.hasbi.n: It is authentically a Companion statement, and its words are in the Quran (al-Tawbah 9:129).
§a.afw.m: O Allah, I ask You for pardon and wellbeing in this world and the Hereafter. O Allah, I ask You for pardon and wellbeing in my religion, my worldly affairs, my family and my wealth. O Allah, cover my faults and calm my fears. O Allah, guard me from in front of me and behind me, from my right and my left, and from above me, and I seek refuge in Your greatness from being taken unawares from beneath me.
§a.afw.v: The Prophet ﷺ never left these supplications in the evening and the morning.
§a.afw.s: Abu Dawud (5074) and Ibn Majah (3871); graded authentic by al-Albani in Sahih Ibn Majah (2/332)
§a.alim.m: O Allah, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Lord and Sovereign of all things, I bear witness that there is no god but You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my soul and from the evil of Satan and his call to associate partners with You, and from bringing evil upon myself or upon any Muslim.
§a.alim.v: The Prophet ﷺ taught it to Abu Bakr to say in the morning, in the evening and on going to bed.
§a.alim.s: Al-Tirmidhi (3392) and Abu Dawud (5067); see Sahih al-Tirmidhi (3/142)
§a.bismillah.m: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
§a.bismillah.v: Whoever says it three times in the morning and three times in the evening, nothing will harm him.
§a.bismillah.s: Abu Dawud (5088), al-Tirmidhi (3388) and Ibn Majah (3869); Ibn Baz graded its chain good in Tuhfat al-Akhyar
§a.radit.m: I am pleased with Allah as my Lord, with Islam as my religion, and with Muhammad ﷺ as my Prophet.
§a.radit.v: Whoever says it three times in the morning and evening, Allah has promised to please him on the Day of Resurrection.
§a.radit.s: Abu Dawud (5072), al-Tirmidhi (3389) and Ahmad (4/337); graded good by Ibn Baz in Tuhfat al-Akhyar
§a.radit.n: The words themselves are authentic in Sahih Muslim (386), said on hearing the call to prayer.
§a.hayy.m: O Ever-Living, O Sustainer of all, by Your mercy I seek help. Set right all my affairs, and do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye.
§a.hayy.v: The Prophet ﷺ advised Fatimah to say it every morning and evening.
§a.hayy.s: Al-Hakim (1/545), who graded it authentic with al-Dhahabi agreeing; graded good by al-Albani in Sahih al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (1/273)
§a.fath.m: We have entered the morning, and all sovereignty belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, I ask You for the good of this day: its victory, its help, its light, its blessing and its guidance, and I seek refuge in You from the evil in it and the evil after it.
§a.fath.e: We have entered the evening, and all sovereignty belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, I ask You for the good of this night: its victory, its help, its light, its blessing and its guidance, and I seek refuge in You from the evil in it and the evil after it.
§a.fath.s: Abu Dawud (5084); Shuayb and Abd al-Qadir al-Arnaut graded its chain good in their edition of Zad al-Maad (2/273)
§a.fitra.m: We have entered the morning upon the natural way of Islam, upon the word of sincere faith, upon the religion of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and upon the way of our father Ibrahim, upright and submitting, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah.
§a.fitra.e: We have entered the evening upon the natural way of Islam, upon the word of sincere faith, upon the religion of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and upon the way of our father Ibrahim, upright and submitting, and he was not of those who associate partners with Allah.
§a.fitra.s: Ahmad (3/406–407) and Ibn al-Sunni in Amal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (34); see Sahih al-Jami (4/209)
§a.subhan.m: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him.
§a.subhan.v: Whoever says it a hundred times in the morning and evening, no one will bring anything better on the Day of Resurrection except one who said the same or more.
§a.tahlil10.m: There is no god but Allah alone, without partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things.
§a.tahlil10.v: Ten times, or once when tired; whoever says it ten times is like one who freed four souls from the descendants of Ismail.
§a.tahlil10.s: Sahih Muslim (2693); see Sahih al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (1/272)
§a.tahlil100.m: There is no god but Allah alone, without partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things.
§a.tahlil100.v: A hundred times in the morning: it equals freeing ten slaves, a hundred good deeds are written for him, a hundred sins are erased, and it protects him from Satan that day until evening.
§a.adad.m: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, as many times as the number of His creation, as much as pleases Him, as heavy as His Throne, and as much as the ink of His words.
§a.adad.v: The Prophet ﷺ said them to Juwayriyah after the dawn prayer, and said that they would outweigh all she had said since morning.
§a.ilm.m: O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good provision and accepted deeds.
§a.ilm.v: The Prophet ﷺ used to say it after finishing the dawn prayer.
§a.ilm.s: Ibn Majah (925) and Ibn al-Sunni (54); graded authentic by al-Albani in Sahih Ibn Majah
§a.istighfar.m: I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance.
§a.istighfar.v: The Prophet ﷺ used to seek Allah's forgiveness and repent to Him a hundred times a day.
§a.kalimat.m: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
§a.kalimat.v: Whoever says it in the evening will not be harmed by any sting that night.
§a.kalimat.s: Sahih Muslim (2709), Ahmad (2/290) and al-Nasai in Amal al-Yawm wa al-Laylah (590)
§a.salat.m: O Allah, send blessings and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad.
§a.salat.v: Whoever sends blessings on me ten times in the morning and ten in the evening will receive my intercession on the Day of Resurrection.
§a.salat.s: Al-Tabarani; see Majma al-Zawaid (10/120) and Sahih al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib (1/273)
§a.salat.n: Its chain is disputed; the virtue of sending blessings on the Prophet ﷺ is authentic in Sahih Muslim (408).
دعا نوحٌ عليه السلام قومَه إلى عبادة الل: Noah (peace be upon him) called his people to worship Allah alone for a very long time: a thousand years less fifty. He was patient and never gave up.
أمره الله أن يصنع سفينة كبيرة، فكان قومه: Allah commanded him to build a large ship. His people passed by and mocked him, but he kept working with trust and certainty.
ولما جاء أمر الله، حمل في السفينة من كل: When Allah's command came, he carried in the ship a pair of every kind of animal, and the believers with him, and said: In the name of Allah is its course and its anchorage.
جاء الطوفان، فجرت السفينة بمن فيها في مو: The flood came, and the ship sailed with everyone aboard through waves like mountains, and Allah kept them safe.
ثم أمر الله الأرض أن تبلع ماءها، والسماء: Then Allah commanded the earth to swallow its water and the sky to stop, and the ship came to rest safely on Mount Judi.
Being patient in doing good, however long it takes.
We obey Allah even if people make fun of us.
Safety comes with faith and good deeds.
كم سنة لبث نوح يدعو قومه؟: How many years did Noah call his people?
أين رست السفينة؟: Where did the ship come to rest?
ماذا حمل نوح في السفينة؟: What did Noah carry in the ship?
من كل زوجين اثنين والمؤمنين: A pair of every kind, and the believers
كان قوم إبراهيم عليه السلام يعبدون تماثي: Abraham's people (peace be upon him) worshipped statues they had made with their own hands. He asked them: What are these statues to which you are devoted?
فلما خرجوا، كسّر الأصنام كلها إلا كبيرها: When they went out, he broke all the idols except the biggest one, so that they would think and return to the truth.
سألوه: أأنت فعلت هذا؟ قال: بل فعله كبيره: They asked him: Did you do this? He said: Rather, this biggest one of them did it, so ask them, if they can speak. And they knew within themselves that idols cannot help and cannot speak.
غضبوا وألقوه في نار عظيمة، فقال الله: يا: They grew angry and threw him into a huge fire, and Allah said: O fire, be coolness and safety for Abraham. And he came out of it unharmed.
Only Allah deserves to be worshipped.
We use our minds, ask questions and think.
Whoever relies on Allah, Allah protects him.
ماذا قال الله للنار؟: What did Allah say to the fire?
لماذا كسر الأصنام؟: Why did he break the idols?
ليفكّر قومه أنها لا تنفع: So his people would think and see that they are useless
يونس عليه السلام رسول من الله. خرج من بل: Jonah (peace be upon him) was a messenger of Allah. He left his town angry with his people and boarded a ship full of people.
اضطربت السفينة، فاقترعوا فوقعت القرعة عل: The ship was in trouble, so they cast lots, and the lot fell on him. He was thrown into the sea, and a huge whale swallowed him.
في ظلمات الليل والبحر وبطن الحوت نادى: ل: In the darkness of the night, the sea and the whale, he called out: There is no god but You, glory be to You; I was indeed among the wrongdoers.
ولأنه كان من المسبّحين نجّاه الله، فألقا: Because he was one of those who glorified Allah, Allah saved him. The whale cast him onto the shore while he was ill, and Allah made a gourd plant grow over him.
ثم أرسله الله إلى قومه وهم مائة ألف أو ي: Then Allah sent him to his people, a hundred thousand or more. They all believed, and Allah let them enjoy life for a time.
ندعو الله في كل وقت، وهو يسمعنا حتى في ا: We call on Allah at every moment, and He hears us even in the dark.
We admit our mistakes and turn back to Allah.
Being patient and not getting angry.
ماذا قال يونس في بطن الحوت؟: What did Jonah say inside the whale?
لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمي: There is no god but You, glory be to You; I was indeed among the wrongdoers
ماذا أنبت الله عليه؟: What did Allah make grow over him?
خافت أم موسى على طفلها من فرعون، فألهمها: Moses' mother feared for her baby because of Pharaoh, so Allah inspired her: Nurse him, and when you fear for him, put him in the river, and do not fear or grieve; We will return him to you.
حمل الماءُ الصندوقَ فالتقطه آل فرعون، فق: The water carried the box, and Pharaoh's family picked it up. Pharaoh's wife said: A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us.
قالت أم موسى لأخته: تتبّعي أثره، فراقبته: Moses' mother said to his sister: Follow him. She watched him from afar, and the baby refused every nurse.
فدلّتهم أخته على أهل بيت يكفلونه، فردّه: His sister told them of a household that would care for him, so Allah returned him to his mother, that she might be content and not grieve, and know that Allah's promise is true.
Allah's promise is true and never fails.
Trusting Allah when we are afraid.
A clever sister helps her family.
أين وضعت أم موسى طفلها؟: Where did Moses' mother put her baby?
في صندوق في النهر: In a box on the river
قرة عين لي ولك لا تقتلوه: A comfort of the eye for me and for you; do not kill him
لماذا رُدّ موسى إلى أمه؟: Why was Moses returned to his mother?
كي تقرّ عينها ولا تحزن: So she would be content and not grieve
ورث سليمانُ أباه داود عليهما السلام، وعل: Solomon inherited from his father David (peace be upon them both). Allah taught him the language of birds and gave him of all things.
وجُمع لسليمان جنوده من الجن والإنس والطي: Solomon's soldiers of jinn, men and birds were gathered for him, and they marched in wonderful order.
فلما أتوا على وادي النمل قالت نملة: يا أ: When they came to the Valley of the Ants, an ant said: O ants, enter your homes so that Solomon and his soldiers do not crush you without noticing.

نزل القرآن الكريم على النبي ﷺ من عند الل: The Noble Quran was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ from Allah through Gabriel (peace be upon him). The verses show that its revelation began in Ramadan, on the Night of Decree, and then it came down in parts, as events required, over about twenty-three years, so that Allah would strengthen the Prophet's heart and it would be recited to people at a measured pace.
ابتداء النزول في رمضان، في ليلة مباركة ه: Revelation began in Ramadan, on a blessed night: the Night of Decree.
نزل منجّماً (مفرّقاً) لا جملة واحدة، وذك: It came down in instalments, not all at once. Scholars mention among the wisdoms: strengthening the Prophet's heart ﷺ, easing memorisation and understanding, and the gradual giving of rulings.
الواسطة في النزول جبريل عليه السلام، الر: The bearer of revelation was Gabriel (peace be upon him), the Trustworthy Spirit.
اعتنى العلماء بمعرفة أول ما نزل من القرآ: Scholars took care to know the first and the last of the Quran to be revealed, since this shows the history and gradual order of the rulings and distinguishes the abrogating from the abrogated. The soundest view is that the opening of Surah Al-Alaq was revealed first, then the opening of Surah Al-Muddaththir after a pause in revelation. They differed over the last revealed, with several views, among them the verse "And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah".
أول ما نزل على الإطلاق: «اقرأ باسم ربك ا: The very first revealed: "Read in the name of your Lord who created" up to "taught man what he did not know".
After the pause in revelation, the opening of Surah Al-Muddaththir came down.
في آخر ما نزل أقوال، ولا يُرفع منها قول: There are several views on the last revealed. None is explicitly attributed to the Prophet ﷺ; each reflects what a Companion knew.
المشهور عند العلماء أن المكي ما نزل قبل: The well-known view among scholars is that Makki is what was revealed before the Hijra and Madani what was revealed after it, even if in Makkah. This is known by transmission from the Companions and their Successors, not by reasoning alone. It helps in knowing abrogation, the history of the rulings, and the style of the call in each stage.
يغلب على المكي: الدعوة إلى التوحيد والبع: Makki passages mostly call to monotheism and the Resurrection, tell the stories of the prophets, have short verses, and address "O mankind".
يغلب على المدني: تفصيل الأحكام والحدود و: Madani passages mostly detail rulings, penalties and jihad, mention the People of the Book and the hypocrites, and address "O you who believe".
في عدد من السور خلاف بين العلماء في كونه: Scholars differ over whether some surahs are Makki or Madani, and some surahs contain excepted verses.
سبب النزول: ما نزلت الآية أو الآيات متحد: An occasion of revelation is an event or question that a verse or verses came down about, or whose ruling they explained, at the time it happened. It can only be known through sound reports from those who witnessed the revelation. Knowing it helps in understanding the verse and removing confusion, and according to most scholars the ruling follows the general wording, not the specific occasion.
لا يُعرف سبب النزول بالرأي، وإنما بالروا: Occasions of revelation are not known by opinion, only by sound reports from the Companions.
قد يتعدد السبب والنازل واحد، وقد تنزل آي: One passage may have several occasions, and several passages may share one occasion.
العبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب، فيشمل: The ruling follows the general wording, not the specific occasion, so it covers everyone in the same situation.
جُمع القرآن ثلاث مرات: في عهد النبي ﷺ حف: The Quran was compiled three times: in the Prophet's time ﷺ, memorised in hearts and written on parchment, palm stalks and stone tablets; in the time of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, gathered into sheets after many reciters were martyred at al-Yamama; and in the time of Uthman ibn Affan, copied into mushafs in the dialect of Quraysh and sent to the major cities. Allah Himself has guaranteed its preservation.

الجمع الثاني في عهد أبي بكر: جمع ما كُتب: Second compilation, under Abu Bakr: what had been written was gathered into one set of sheets on Umar's advice, a task entrusted to Zayd ibn Thabit.

For this Allah has varied every kind of parable in the Quran and made parables a path to remembrance and understanding.

مثل نوره كمشكاة: The parable of His light is like a niche
تمثيل مركّب: مشكاة فيها مصباح، في زجاجة: A compound parable: a niche with a lamp, in a glass like a brilliant star, lit from the oil of a blessed tree; light upon light.

تختصر الاستعارة الصورة في كلمة، وتلمّح ا: Metaphor condenses an image into one word, metonymy hints at a meaning through what accompanies it with refinement and discretion, and personification breathes life into the inanimate and into time: the day is "stripped" from the night, the dawn "breathes", and humility becomes a "wing" that is lowered.
واشتعل الرأس شيباً: My head has blazed with grey
شبّه انتشار الشيب في الرأس باشتعال النار: The spread of grey hair is likened to the blaze of fire, condensing all of old age into three words.
جناح الذل من الرحمة: The wing of humility out of mercy
صورة الطائر يخفض جناحه لفراخه رحمة وحنوا: The image of a bird lowering its wing over its young in tenderness clothes kindness to parents in mercy.
والصبح إذا تنفس: And the dawn when it breathes
الليل يعسعس مقبلاً ومدبراً، والصبح يتنفس: The night approaches and departs, and the dawn breathes as a living being breathes after constriction: personification that turns time into a living creature.
نسلخ منه النهار: We strip the day from it
جُعل ذهاب الضوء كسلخ الجلد عن الذبيحة، ف: The departure of light is made like stripping a hide, so the night appears as the original and the day as a covering over it.
أُسندت الإرادة إلى الجدار لميله وإشرافه: "Wanting" is ascribed to the wall because it leaned on the verge of falling, so the scene itself speaks of danger.
يد مغلولة وبسط كل البسط: A chained hand and a hand fully open
كناية عن البخل بالغلّ، وعن الإسراف بالبس: Miserliness pictured as a chained hand and extravagance as a hand fully open, then the image of sitting blamed and destitute.

اللباس ستر ودفء وقرب وزينة؛ صورة واحدة ت: A garment covers, warms, stays close and adorns: one image gathering the meanings of affection between spouses, together with a refined allusion to intimacy.

صُورت الغيبة بأبشع صورة تنفر منها الطباع: Backbiting is pictured in the most repulsive image nature recoils from, so the listener hates it by law as he hates that by instinct.
المشاهد الكونية: جمال الخلق المنظور: Cosmic scenes: the visible beauty of creation
يدعو القرآن إلى النظر في الكون نظرة تأمل: The Quran invites us to look at the universe with reflection and wonder: the built and adorned sky, the raised mountains, the outspread earth, the driven clouds, the plants that stir and swell. In a single verse it joins the proof of power to the delight of beauty.
أفلا ينظرون إلى الإبل كيف خلقت: Do they not look at the camels, how they are created?
أربع لوحات في مشهد البادية: الإبل، والسم: Four panels of the desert scene: camels, sky, mountains and earth. The Arab saw them every day, and the Quran invites him to see them anew.
السماء بنيناها وزيناها: We built the sky and adorned it
سماء بلا فروج، وأرض ممدودة، وزوج بهيج، و: A sky without rifts, an outspread earth, every delightful kind, and tall palms with clustered spathes: words that carry beauty as they carry proof.

أمر صريح بالنظر إلى الثمر في أطواره حتى: An explicit command to look at fruit through its stages until it ripens: contemplating beauty is worship the Quran calls to.

مشهد متتابع الحركة: سوق السحاب، ثم تأليف: A scene of successive movement: driving the clouds, joining them, piling them up, rain pouring from within, and lightning that almost takes away sight.

الرياح تثير، والسحاب يُبسط ويُجعل كسفاً،: The winds stir, the clouds spread and break into fragments, rain falls from within, then the joy of those who receive it.

مشاهد القيامة: Scenes of the Day of Resurrection

إذا الشمس كورت: When the sun is wrapped up

الناس كالفراش المبثوث في حيرته وتهافته،: People like scattered moths in their confusion and rushing, mountains like fluffed wool in their lightness: two similes that turn the image of strength into weakness.
تذهل كل مرضعة عما أرضعت: Every nursing mother will forget her infant
أقوى العواطف وأرسخها تنقطع من الهول، وتر: The strongest and firmest of emotions is cut off by terror, and you see people as if drunk while they are not drunk.

الصاخة تصك الآذان، ثم مشهد الفرار بترتيب: The Deafening Blast strikes the ears, then the scene of flight, ascending from brother to mother and father, then wife and children.
كأنهم جراد منتشر: As if they were scattered locusts
خروج الناس من القبور في كثرتهم واضطرابهم: People coming out of their graves in their multitude, agitation and spread like locusts, with their eyes humbled.
الجبال تحسبها جامدة وهي تمضي مضي السحاب،: You think the mountains are still while they pass as clouds pass: the scene joins apparent stillness to hidden motion.
فإذا نفخ في الصور نفخة واحدة: When the Horn is blown with a single blast
نفخة واحدة تُحمل بها الأرض والجبال فتدكا: One blast, and the earth and mountains are lifted and crushed with a single crushing, and the sky splits, frail on that Day.
يصور القرآن خلجات النفس كما يصور مشاهد ا: The Quran portrays the stirrings of the soul as it portrays the scenes of the universe: a chest so constricted it is as if climbing into the sky, the wide earth narrowing for the distressed, hearts reaching the throats in fear, a mother's heart becoming empty, and the wrongdoer biting his hands in regret.
كأنما يصعد في السماء: As though climbing into the sky
انشراح الصدر للهدى يقابله صدر ضيق حرج، ك: A chest opened to guidance is set against a chest tight and constricted, like one straining to climb into the sky with his breath growing short.
ضاقت عليهم الأرض بما رحبت: The earth closed in on them despite its vastness
حال الثلاثة الذين خُلّفوا: الأرض على سعت: The state of the three who were left behind: the earth, vast as it is, closed in, and their own souls closed in, until they were certain there was no refuge except in Allah.
تصوير لشدة الخوف يوم الأحزاب: زاغت الأبص: A portrayal of extreme fear on the day of the Confederates: eyes shifted and hearts almost left their places.

قلب خلا من كل شيء إلا من ذكر ولدها، حتى: A heart emptied of everything except thought of her child, so that she nearly revealed him, had Allah not strengthened her heart.
حزن يعقوب عليه السلام صُور أثراً في العي: Jacob's grief is pictured as a mark on the eye and as suppressed sorrow in the heart that complains to none but Allah.

صورة النفس بين الجزع عند الشر والمنع عند: A portrait of the soul between panic in hardship and withholding in ease, after which the Quran makes an exception of those who pray.

الإنسان في الضر يدعو على كل أحواله، فإذا: In hardship man calls on Allah in every posture; once relieved, he passes on as if he had never called: a true picture of the soul's fickleness.
الجمال والزينة في القرآن: Beauty and adornment in the Quran
ذكر القرآن الجمال والزينة في الخلق والنع: The Quran mentions beauty and adornment in creation and its blessings: the beauty of livestock when they return in the evening and go out in the morning, the adornment of stars in the sky, gardens full of delight, and Allah perfecting the form of man. It permits adornment to His servants and makes the adornment of the earth a test, not an end.

جواب القسم بالتين والزيتون وطور سينين وا: The answer to the oath by the fig, the olive, Mount Sinai and the secure city: man was created in the most balanced form and shape.

لم يقصر القرآن الجمال على الصور، بل وصف: The Quran does not limit beauty to forms; it describes the acts of the soul with it: beautiful patience with no complaint except to Allah, beautiful pardon with no reproach, beautiful distancing with no harm, and a beautiful release that preserves dignity at parting. It calls to repel evil with what is better.
قالها يعقوب عليه السلام حين جاؤوا على قم: Jacob said it when they brought Joseph's shirt with false blood, then sought Allah's help.
فصبر جميل عسى الله أن يأتيني بهم جميعاً: Beautiful patience; perhaps Allah will bring them all to me
تكررت الكلمة في المصيبة الثانية، ومعها ا: The phrase is repeated at the second calamity, now with hope: beautiful patience is inseparable from thinking well of Allah.
فاصبر صبراً جميلاً: So be patient with a beautiful patience
أمر للنبي ﷺ بالصبر على أذى قومه صبراً لا: A command to the Prophet ﷺ to bear his people's harm with patience free of panic and weariness.
فاصفح الصفح الجميل: So pardon with a beautiful pardon
الصفح الجميل: عفو بلا أذى، يقابل الإساءة: Beautiful pardon: forgiving without harm, meeting wrong with kindness.
واهجرهم هجراً جميلاً: And leave them with a beautiful leaving
حتى الهجر له جمال: إعراض بلا عتاب ولا أذ: Even distancing has its beauty: turning away without reproach or harm.
وسرحوهن سراحاً جميلاً: And release them with a beautiful release
الفراق نفسه يُطلب فيه الجمال: متعة وإحسا: Beauty is required even in parting: a gift, kindness and preserved dignity.
صورة العدو يتحول ولياً حميماً بالإحسان،: The image of an enemy becoming a devoted friend through kindness; none attains it but one of great fortune.
وقولوا للناس حسناً: And speak to people good words
جمال القول من جملة الميثاق المأخوذ على ب: Beautiful speech is part of the covenant taken from the Children of Israel, alongside tawhid and kindness to parents.
إلحاق أمر بأمر في صفة جامعة بينهما، فيُر: Joining one thing to another through a shared quality, so an abstract meaning is seen in a tangible form: the light of faith is a lamp in a niche, the good word is a good tree.

تشبيه طُوي أحد طرفيه، فتُنقل الكلمة إلى: A simile with one side folded away, so a word carries a new meaning and the whole image is condensed into one expression: the head "blazes" with grey hair as fire blazes.
Example: "And my head has filled (blazed) with white."
التعبير عن المعنى بلازمه، فيُفهم المقصود: Expressing a meaning through what accompanies it, so the intent is grasped from its image without being stated: a hand chained to the neck pictures extreme miserliness.
Example: "And do not make your hand chained to your neck."

تمثيل نبوي بالحواس: الريح للظاهر والطعم: A prophetic parable through the senses: scent for the outward and taste for the inward. The Quran perfumes its reciter outwardly, and faith sweetens him inwardly.
مثلي ومثل الأنبياء كرجل بنى بيتاً فأحسنه: My example and that of the prophets: a man who built a beautiful house
صورة بناء جميل كامل إلا لبنة، فكانت الرس: The image of a beautiful, complete building missing one brick: the final message completed its beauty.
مثل المؤمنين في توادهم كمثل الجسد: The believers in their mutual love are like one body
تشبيه الجماعة بالجسد الواحد يصور التراحم: Likening the community to one body makes compassion tangible: when one limb aches, the whole body stays awake for it.
إن الله جميل يحب الجمال: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty
حب الجمال في الثوب والنعل ليس كبراً؛ فال: Loving beauty in clothing and footwear is not arrogance: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty, while arrogance is rejecting the truth and despising people.

الجمال الذي يُوزن عند الله جمال القلب وا: The beauty weighed by Allah is the beauty of the heart and of deeds; forms and wealth are not what reward depends on.

الإحسان جمال الفعل في كل شيء، حتى في الذ: Excellence is the beauty of action in everything, even in slaughter, so how much more in dealing with people?

No authentic text from the Prophet fixes these verses to a number or a manner; they are grouped only because they share the word "healing".
